focus: Windows: Git Bash resolution, paths with spaces, process-tree kill, PowerShell hooks

findings.title: TECH-SPEC has no Windows shell-resolution rule; it would re-break three chained v1 fixes
findings.claim: TECH-SPEC §ctx_execute (line 437) and PRD §8 ('runtimes found on PATH') give no algorithm for choosing a shell on Windows. v1 needed three linked fixes to get this right, none of which are named in any v2 doc: (1) resolveWindowsBash must prefer canonical Git Bash paths and must skip WSL/WindowsApps bash shims, falling back to `where bash` and then to pwsh; (2) native git calls need MSYS path conversion preserved, but ctx_execute child processes for other tools (e.g. mvn) need it suppressed, so the fix is tool-specific, not global; (3) a naive PATH lookup finds the wrong bash first on a stock Windows runner.
findings.evidence: git -C cm-main log --oneline --all shows 65012337 'gate Windows bash detection through where bash so pwsh fallback is reachable' (msg: 'resolveWindowsBash() probed the well-known Git Bash paths with existsSync() BEFORE consulting where bash... when where bash yields no real candidate, return null... when where bash surfaces a Git Bash candidate we still canonicalize to the absolute Git\usr\bin\bash.exe path (WSL/WindowsApps skipped) so native git keeps MSYS path conversion'); e2bce0b5 'preserve Git Bash path conversion for native git (#826)'; 89f4e736 '#782: ...Rewrite the bare mvn token to mvn.cmd... This avoids re-enabling global MSYS path-conversion suppression that #826/#791 removed for native git.' grep over docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md and docs/v2/adr/*.md for MinGW|MSYS|WindowsApps|resolveWindowsBash|where bash returns zero matches. docs/v2/review/REVIEW-r2.md:25 already flagged the PATH-lookup/WSL-WindowsApps half of this gap against PRD-v2.md:192 and asked for 'the exact Windows bash-resolution rule' to be added to TECH-SPEC §8; TECH-SPEC §437 as it stands today still does not contain it, so the r2 ask was not closed, and the tool-specific MSYS-suppression-vs-preservation split (mvn vs git) was never raised in r2 at all.
findings.fix: Add a Windows shell-resolution subsection to TECH-SPEC (near GP4/§8): specify resolveWindowsBash's order (canonical Git Bash path check -> `where bash` with WSL/WindowsApps candidates excluded -> pwsh fallback), state that MSYS path conversion is preserved only for native git invocations and suppressed for other child commands (rewrite bare launcher tokens like `mvn` to their `.cmd` form instead of a global suppression toggle), and add a GP4 Windows case with WSL bash first on PATH plus a git call and a non-git call in the same script to prove both rules hold at once.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: e2bce0b5 (2026-06-13, 'preserve Git Bash path conversion for native git #826'), then 89f4e736 (2026-06-21, '#782 + #788'), then 65012337 (2026-06-21, same-day follow-up). ORIGINAL_INTENT: keep git's own MSYS path rewriting working while stopping that same rewriting from breaking other native Windows binaries, and stop a too-eager existsSync probe from hiding a real 'bash unavailable' state from the pwsh fallback. REGRESSION_RISK: a v2 reimplementation of 'runtimes found on PATH' that does a single global MSYS toggle, or that checks existsSync before `where bash`, reproduces the exact two bugs these three commits fixed. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: keep the suppression decision per-invoked-command (git vs everything else), not a process-wide flag; keep the `where bash`-first probe order; keep the WSL/WindowsApps exclusion when canonicalizing a found bash path.

findings.title: v1's Windows ctx_execute cwd unification and temp-dir EBUSY cleanup have no equivalent requirement in TECH-SPEC GP4
findings.claim: TECH-SPEC §437/GP4 lists 'deleted cwd' as a test case but does not require (a) that cwd be unified to the project root across all ctx_execute languages rather than defaulting non-shell runtimes to the sandbox tmp dir, or (b) that sandbox temp-dir removal retry on EBUSY/EPERM from a lingering SQLite -wal/-shm handle on Windows instead of swallowing the error silently.
findings.evidence: git -C cm-main show 89f4e736 -s --format=%B: '#788(a): Non-shell runtimes (python/js/ts/...) ran with cwd=sandbox tmpDir, so repo-relative checks failed depending on language. Unify cwd to the project root...'; '#788(b): .ctx-mode-* temp dirs leaked on Windows when SQLite -wal/-shm handles lingered and a single rmSync threw EBUSY/EPERM into a silent catch. Add cleanupTmpDir() with rmSync maxRetries/retryDelay backoff.' grep over docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md and docs/v2/adr/*.md for EBUSY|retryDelay|maxRetries|cleanupTmp returns zero matches; GP4's bullet list (line 292) names 'deleted cwd' only, not cwd-unification-across-languages or tmp-dir retry-on-EBUSY.
findings.fix: Add two GP4 sub-cases: (1) a non-shell language (python/js) call on Windows asserting cwd equals the project root, not a sandbox tmp dir; (2) a Windows-only case that opens context.db (leaving -wal/-shm handles live) then runs ctx_execute and asserts the sandbox temp dir is removed without a swallowed EBUSY/EPERM, i.e. the cleanup retries rather than silently leaking the dir.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 89f4e736 (2026-06-21, '#788(a) and #788(b)'). ORIGINAL_INTENT: make repo-relative path checks behave the same regardless of which ctx_execute language ran them, and stop Windows file-lock timing from leaking temp directories. REGRESSION_RISK: a v2 rewrite of the sandbox runner that re-introduces a per-language default cwd, or a plain rmSync without retry, reopens both leaks on Windows CI. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: cwd default must be the project root (or an explicit per-call override) for every language, not just shell; temp-dir teardown must retry past EBUSY/EPERM rather than catch-and-ignore.

covered_and_confirmed_ok: ADR-0010's doctor golden-test list keeps 'a path that contains a space' as a required case, matching v1's #548/#549 quoted-pluginRoot fix (verified: git -C cm-main show 3434b18e, 'quote pluginRoot in generated hook commands so paths with spaces parse correctly #549'); no regression found here.

DECISIONS-r3 Q8 / TECH-SPEC line 437 settle process-tree kill as Windows Job Object, which is a stated owner decision (not a doc contradiction) and is a stronger primitive than v1's taskkill /F /T /PID (git -C cm-main show 8a778ba9); no finding raised against this decision per task rules.
